text:
THE KENYA NATIONAL EXAMINATIONS COUNCIL
 SCHOOL BASED ASSESSMENT
 Physical and Health Education
 Grade 6 – 2022 (Regular)
 SECTION B: PERFORMANCE TASKS (15 marks)
 INSTRUCTIONS TO THE TEACHER
 1. This section of grade 6 PHE SBA consists of performance-based assessment tasks (Task
 2 and Task 3). Section A (Task 1-Written task) will be uploaded and administered later
 as per the circular to schools on the administration of 2022 SBA.
 2. Performance based assessment tasks have been uploaded in advance to minimize pressure
 of time and enable teachers assess learners effectively.
 3. The assessment tasks are to be undertaken by all learners in Grade 6
 4. Section B consists of two performance assessment tasks (Task 2 and Task 3)
 i. Task 2: Performance task: Two handed catch (8 marks)
 ii. Task 3: Performance task: Rope Work- Partner Rope work (7 marks)
 5. Each learner should be scored individually as they perform the tasks
 6. Use the checklists provided to assess each learner
 7. Scoring guides provided shall be used to rate the learner’s performance
 8. Learners with disabilities should be assessed using the adapted assessment tools provided.
 Teachers may modify the adaptations suggested based on individual learner’s needs but
 should not compromise the assessment of the outcome targeted.
 9. Teachers at the school should collaborate where necessary to ensure successful
 administration and conduct of the assessment.
 10. The teacher to:
 a. familiarize with the tool before administration.
 b. use the appropriate mode of communication when instructing the learner.
 c. guide and support the learner accordingly in the performance of all tasks.
 d. ensure that the assessment is done within the prescribed period.
 e. organize for advance provision of materials required for the assessment.
 f. use improvised or available materials where necessary.
 g. always ensure the safety of each learner during the assessment.
 h. share and discuss the assessment instructions with the learners to know what is
 expected of them.
 i. maintain evidence of each learner’s performance in ALL the tasks for reference
 and quality assurance.
PHE 1

 SECTION B: PERFORMANCE TASKS (15 marks)
 Task 2: Two-handed catch in Handball (8 marks)
 Instructions to the teacher
 The teacher to:
 i. Identify safe space for the performance of tasks.
 ii. provide an appropriate ball(s)/improvised ball(s)/adapted ball(s) where necessary
 iii. Organize learners in pairs or in groups of 5-10 members.
 iv. Mark a point on the ground showing where learners will be receiving the ball from.
 v. Instruct learners to stand in a linear formation(s) behind each other or in a semi-circle.
 If learners are in pars, they could stand approximately 3 to 5 metres apart facing each
 other.
 vi. Instruct one learner/the thrower/feeder/teacher to stand approximately 3 to 5 metres with
 the ball and face the team members.
 vii. Instruct the learner with the ball/ the thrower/feeder/teacher to throw it to the first learner
 on the line. The first learner to make a two-handed catch and return the ball to the
 feeder/ the thrower.
 viii. Give each learner a maximum of three chances to make a two-handed catch
 ix. Assess each learner’s competency in performing a two-handed catch using the
 checklist provided
PHE 2
School Based Assessment Grade 6 ©2022 The Kenya National Examinations Council
 Checklist for Assessing Learner’s competency in performing the two-handed catch in
 Handball
 Skills to be assessed Descriptor Marks
 1. Ready Stance Legs slightly apart 1
 position Position of the Hands in front of the body at the chest level,
 hands fingers spread forming a ‘W’ shape
 Eye focus Eye should focus on the ball 1
 2. Execution Hands Stretch both arms towards the oncoming ball
 (catching) movement
 Leg movement Step forward with one leg as hands are being
 outstretched
 Catch Receive the ball on the palm and hold it firmly
 with fingers forming a “W” shape
 3. Recovery Hands/Legs Draw the arms close to the chest to cushion the
 movement ball as you step back with the leading foot
 4. Core Self-efficacy Self-confidence, self-esteem, readiness to perform,
 competency self-appreciation
 Total Marks
PHE 3
School Based Assessment Grade 6 ©2022 The Kenya National Examinations Council
 Task 3: Rope Work: Partner Work (7 Marks)
 Instructions to the teacher
 The teacher to:
 i. Ensure safety of all learners.
 ii. Arrange for the availability of adequate safe space.
 iii. Guide the learners to pair up appropriately.
 iv. Guide the pairs to perform rope skipping while facing one another.
 v. Use the checklist provided to assess the learner’s competency in performing partner
 work in rope work
 vi. Instruct the rope turner to exchange with the partner at appropriate time so that each will
 get a chance to be assessed in all the aspects.
 vii. Use the scoring guide provided to rate the learner’s performance
 viii.
 Checklist to assess the learner’s competency in rope work partner work
 Skills to be assessed Descriptor Marks
 1. Stance Partners facing one another at arm’s length distance 1
 Ready Position of the Feet comfortably apart and flat on the ground
 position feet
 Rope grip The rope turner holds the rope tightly with both hands
 at the waist height behind the body
 2. Execution The start The rope turner to give clear communication before
 turning the rope “Ready, Go”
 Coordination Jumping the rope in unison, establishing a rhythm 1
 Sustained Jump continuously 10 times while the turner
 activity maintains a steady rope turning tempo.
 3. Core Unity Turn taking, respecting each other, appreciating
 value others’ efforts, sharing resources, accepting the roles 1
 assigned
 Total Marks 07
